_about: 727-200F, from Boeing D6-58324, 727 Airplane Characteristics for Airport Planning (June 1978, revised May 2011; the copy on boeing.com's airport planning page) 2.2 General Dimensions, Model 727-200 (page index 18): side, plan and front views on one sheet, a scan of about 40 px a meter drawn on graph paper. Pixels of layers.py rasters at scale 5, line centres. Scaled by the printed 41.50 m (136 ft 2 in) from the nose to the tail cone. A T-tail (`stabilizer.mount`), two JT8D nacelles on the rear fuselage on stub pylons (`engines.mount`), and the third in the tail cone fed by an S-duct from an intake on the crown ahead of the fin (`tailEngine`, duct s). The front view draws the tailplane 0.5 m low against the fuselage: its height is the side view's (`stabilizerZ`). The freighter: no cabin windows; its main-deck cargo door (left) is the 727-100C's from 2.7 (10.67 m to its middle, 3.40 m wide, 2.18 m tall, its sill 5 cm above the entry door's: 727-200F conversions fit the same size of door just aft of the entry door); the entry door (left), forward galley service door (right) and lower-deck cargo doors (right) at 2.7's 727-200 table (5.03 m, 6.78 m, 11.68 m and 27.2 m to their middles), their sills from 2.3's and 2.7's ground-to-sill heights against the entry door's as drawn; the overwing exits and aft galley door, deactivated on freighters, left out. Heights checked against 2.3: the fin's top J less the crown L (middles of their ranges). The printed fuselage heights are 4.01 m (13 ft 2 in) over the cabin and 4.27 m (14 ft) over the wing's belly fairing; the check's middle third is the latter (the side draws the cabin's tube 3.99 m), so no height fit.

windows.note: The 727-200F has no cabin windows (plugged in the conversion).

sources.title: Boeing, 727 Airplane Characteristics for Airport Planning (D6-58324, June 1978, revised May 2011), 2.2 General Dimensions: Model 727-200, 2.3 Ground Clearances, 2.7 Door Clearances: Models 727-100, -100C and 727-200
sources.note: Dimensions and outlines read off the side, plan and front views of 2.2 (tools/trace/b722/); the figures are the aircraft's measurements, not a copy of the drawing. The sheet is a 1978 scan drawn on graph paper, about 40 px a meter: the grid's lines run through the drawing (the nose's crown along one is placed by hand). Scaled by the printed 41.50 m to the tail cone, its overall length, span and width are within 0.7% of their printed figures; its plan draws the tailplane 3.2% short of the printed 10.90 m and the side nacelles 2.75 m out against the printed 2.82 m (the front view's inlet), and its front view draws what stands beside and above the fuselage 0.25-0.5 m low against the fuselage's circle, so the tailplane's height is the side view's. A T-tail, two JT8D nacelles on the rear fuselage on stub pylons, and the third engine in the tail cone (engines[0], mount tail, duct s): its S-duct's intake stands on the crown ahead of the fin, the fin's leading edge rising from its top; its outline runs on under the fin's root fairing to the rudder's trailing edge, and its nozzle is the tail cone's last 1.5 m. The freighter (727-200F conversions): no cabin windows; the main-deck cargo door (left) is the 727-100C's from 2.7 (10.67 m to its middle, 3.40 m wide, 2.18 m tall), the size the conversions fit just aft of the entry door; the entry door (left), forward galley service door (right) and lower-deck cargo doors (right) at 2.7's 727-200 table, their sills from its ground-to-sill heights against the entry door's as drawn (the drawing's entry door sits 0.3 m ahead of the table's 5.03 m); the overwing exits and aft galley door, deactivated on freighters, left out. The fin's tip is checked against 2.3's ground clearances (J less L, middles of their ranges: about 0.15 m).
